title: Multimodal precision diagnostics in clinical xenotransplantation
title_zh: 临床异种移植中的多模态精准诊断
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in pig-to-human xenotransplantation have successfully prevented hyperacute rejection of kidney, heart, liver and lung xenografts, marking a milestone long considered a critical barrier. However, these major advances also brought new challenges into focus, as immune-mediated graft injuries including antibody-mediated rejection, T cell-mediated rejection and innate immune activation have been observed in most xenotransplantation procedures to date. Detection and management of these injuries remain a critical bottleneck, as conventional histopathology and standard clinical monitoring lack the sensitivity required to identify subclinical injury early enough to guide timely intervention. This diagnostic gap underscores an urgent need for the development of advanced, multimodal precision diagnostic frameworks to enhance immune surveillance, which will be essential for standardizing clinical protocols and enabling pathogenesis-driven therapeutic intervention. This approach will inform both immunosuppressive regimens and future gene editing strategies aimed at engineering rejection-resistant porcine organs, ultimately prolonging graft survival. Broad adoption of such an integrative strategy will be essential to transition xenotransplantation from an experimental intervention into a safe, scalable and patient-centred clinical therapy. In this Review, we synthesize recent progress in xenotransplantation and position multimodal precision diagnostics as a pivotal strategy to address the remaining immunological and clinical barriers to widespread clinical implementation. Now that hyperacute rejection of pig xenografts can be reliably prevented, subtler immune-mediated graft injuries have emerged that conventional diagnostics often miss; a multimodal precision diagnostic framework is proposed to detect these injuries earlier, guide personalized immunosuppression and inform future gene editing strategies.
abstract_zh: 猪到人异种移植的最新突破成功预防了肾、心、肝和肺异种移植物的超急性排斥，标志着长期被视为关键障碍的里程碑得以跨越。然而，这些重大进展也带来了新的挑战，因为目前大多数异种移植手术中均观察到了包括抗体介导排斥、T细胞介导排斥和先天免疫激活在内的免疫介导的移植物损伤。这些损伤的检测和管理仍是关键瓶颈，常规病理学和标准临床监测缺乏足够的敏感性，无法尽早识别亚临床损伤以指导及时干预。这种诊断差距强调了迫切需要开发先进的多模态精准诊断框架以增强免疫监测，这将是标准化临床方案和实现基于病因的治疗干预所必需的。该方法将同时指导免疫抑制方案和旨在工程化排斥耐受猪器官的未来基因编辑策略，最终延长移植物存活时间。采取这种整合策略的广泛应用，对于将异种移植从实验性干预转变为安全、可扩展且以患者为中心的临床疗法至关重要。在本综述中，我们总结了异种移植的最新进展，并将多模态精准诊断定位为解决异种移植广泛临床实施所面临的剩余免疫学和临床障碍的关键策略。现在猪异种移植物的超急性排斥已能可靠地预防，更微妙的免疫介导移植物损伤已显现，常规诊断常常无法发现；我们提出了一个多模态精准诊断框架，以更早检测这些损伤，指导个体化免疫抑制并为未来的基因编辑策略提供信息。
